_comment: Generated release artifact of The System — Nexus Patch Feed. The Notion Patch Feed is the source of truth; this file is its public read-only projection, regenerated by /broadcast on each patch and by the admin's nightly sync. Do not hand-edit. It is a sanctioned boundary mirror, not a fallback: a player's agent has no route into the admin Nexus, so this is the read path that always works — a plain HTTPS GET of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TechSecWhisperer/ars-infinita-notion/main/feed.json, no browser and no connector required. 'mechanics_version' is the current game-rules version and 'head' is the newest patch below; both names are used verbatim by the boot card and /doctor, which is why both fields exist even when they hold the same value.

patches.title: v1.0.0 — Gate Protocol goes live
patches.player_facing_summary: The System becomes multiplayer-distributable: the Seed, /awaken, /petition, /party, the Patch Feed itself, and the Sigil Check. Existing instances keep their history untouched; new features are usable from today.

patches.title: v1.0.1 — Codex copy: "Story Bank" naming unified
patches.player_facing_summary: Copy-only patch: the XP table line "Story added to Skill Inventory" now reads "Story added to Story Bank" everywhere, matching the database's display name. No XP values, rules, or schemas change.

patches.title: v1.0.2 — Maintenance window (schedule-setup fix incoming)
patches.player_facing_summary: The System is briefly in maintenance while we fix an issue with automated schedule setup during /awaken. Your data is untouched and commands work normally. If your daily briefing didn't switch on after you awakened, that's the known issue — a fix is coming and you'll be prompted to re-run /awaken. You may see a short maintenance note instead of an automated briefing during the window.

patches.title: v1.1.0 — Capability tiers: /vitals, /doctor, and graceful mobile-lite
patches.player_facing_summary: The System now checks what your session can actually do and adapts to it. New /vitals reports your setup's capabilities (desktop vs mobile-lite, whether an agent browser is available); new /doctor runs diagnostics and repairs common issues. On app-only or mobile sessions, commands that need a browser now degrade gracefully with a clear "won't run here" message instead of failing silently. /awaken now walks you through agent-browser setup so the full command set is available. No XP values, levels, or rules change.

patches.title: v1.2.0 — Alpha 2: The Gates Reopen
patches.player_facing_summary: Alpha 2 is here. Gatecrasher I now unlocks at 2 tracked applications — forward-only, so nothing you've already earned is re-locked. Levels 1–4 are now the Tutorial Arc, your onboarding stretch; once it closes you'll see a stated normal daily-XP band so progress reads clearly. New 📅 System Calendar: your daily briefings and reminders now appear as calendar entries you can browse later, not just one-off notifications. The schedule-setup fix shipped: /awaken now creates your Daily Quest Briefing scheduled task — existing players, re-run /awaken once to pick it up. And The System's plugin now installs from the public marketplace repo — one link. Your history and data are untouched.

patches.title: v1.3.0 — Follow-up, refocused (rules adopted; plugin build to follow)
patches.player_facing_summary: Rules change today; the plugin that implements them ships next. ADOPTED NOW: follow-up becomes stage-weighted — chasing an application nobody has answered rarely changes the outcome, so pre-contact quests (Saved, Applied) stop raising overdue flags, debuffs, streak consequences or any "you're late" framing, while post-contact quests (Recruiter Screen and beyond, where a human has replied) keep the tight cadence and become the priority surface. Also adopted: setup will ask which theme you want and refuse to proceed until you answer — no default, no silent fallback; and any number Notion can compute itself will be computed by Notion and read by your agent rather than re-derived, so your Player Card can't drift from your Ledger. NOT YET IN YOUR PLUGIN: until the next plugin build lands, your installed copy still runs the old flat two-day cadence and setup still has no theme question. You may still see follow-up prompts on quests nobody has answered — those are retired by rule, and you can ignore them. Forward-only: no past XP or streak is re-scored, and nothing is required from you. TRUE TODAY: The System is now MIT licensed — free to use, fork and modify.

patches.title: v1.3.1 — The build landed
patches.player_facing_summary: The two changes your v1.3.0 note listed as adopted as rule, not yet in your plugin — stage-weighted follow-up, and the theme question at setup — are now in the installed plugin. Update to receive them. Forward-only: nothing re-scored. (Supersedes the v1.3.0 line saying your copy still ran the flat cadence and had no theme question.)

patches.title: v1.3.8 — Copy corrections, and one version number
patches.player_facing_summary: Two wording corrections to the rule surfaces, no change to how anything scores. First: the rule saying The System never reveals odds now says plainly what your plugin already does — if you ask directly how the Forge works, its odds and its payout, you get a straight answer. That has been true in the shipped command since 31 July; the rule page just hadn't caught up. The System still won't volunteer anything about a roll you didn't win. Second: the XP table row for a development action now names your Competency Matrix, which is what the database is actually called in your workspace, instead of an internal name. The amount is unchanged at 30. Nothing is re-scored and there is nothing to do.

patches.title: v1.3.9 — Codex installer advisory, and a clearer description
patches.player_facing_summary: If you installed The System for the Codex CLI before v1.3.6, check your own skills. Versions up to 1.3.5 installed 27 skills into the shared skills folder and replaced anything already sitting under the same name — so a skill you wrote yourself called status, log, report, browse, doctor or patch may have been overwritten without warning. Nothing in your Notion workspace is affected; this only touched files on your own machine. The installer now refuses to overwrite anything it did not install, and will tell you the exact paths instead. Antigravity installs were never affected. This notice is late because the channel that delivers it compares a version number that four releases had not moved; that is fixed, and this is the first release that could carry it.

patches.title: v1.3.10 — Build your CV the way you want it read
patches.player_facing_summary: Your CV builder now works the way you would expect to be able to ask it. /armor assembles your CV from named sections, so you can rearrange it in plain language — "move my skills above experience", "drop the interests section", "put certifications at the top". Layout presets cover different situations (graduate, career change, technical, academic, and cleared or government roles), and switching between them reorders your sections without changing a word of what they say. /armor now also adapts to where the job is rather than where you are. Resume convention genuinely differs by country, and getting it wrong costs you in both directions: two pages is right in the UK and over-long in the US, a photo is conventional in Germany and can get an application discarded in Australia or the US, and some European employers expect a data-processing consent line. /armor reads the target country from the quest and applies that market's conventions for length, spelling, dates, personal details, referees and work rights — then tells you in one line what it changed, so you can overrule it. Nothing is invented on your behalf: adapting to a market changes how your history is presented, never the facts in it. Forward-only — no XP value, level threshold, badge criterion or unlock rule changed, and nothing you have already earned is re-scored.

patches.title: v2.0.0 — Beta. Setup tells you when it couldn't finish.
patches.player_facing_summary:
The System is in Beta. Nothing about how you play changes, nothing you have earned is re-scored, and there is nothing to do on your side.

What is actually different is setup, which is the part that was quietly failing. At the end of /awaken it writes a small file to your computer so your next session picks The System back up without you explaining it again. On the desktop app that write can fail for one specific reason: the app has no access to your files at all until you connect a folder to the session. Setup used to finish looking successful anyway, and every session afterwards started cold with nothing saying why.

Now /awaken tries the write and checks it landed. If it worked, it tells you where the file is. If it could not, it says so plainly and tells you what to do — connect a folder, then run /awaken again, which is safe to re-run and will not rebuild anything already in your Notion. Everything built in Notion is finished either way; only that last local step is affected.

Also fixed: if /awaken cannot find your duplicated template it used to tell you to ask the Game Admin for the Seed link — a link the setup instructions had already given you. It now points you back to those instructions instead.

On the version jumping to 2.0.0: the first number is a release line, not a warning. Alpha was 1.x, Beta is 2.x. Nothing you have installed stops working because it moved.

patches.title: v2.0.1 — A command can no longer point at something that isn't in your workspace
patches.player_facing_summary:
Commands refer to the databases in your workspace by name. If a command names something your workspace does not have, the rule your agent follows is to stop and log a question rather than guess — which is the safe behaviour, but it means the command quietly does nothing instead of failing loudly.

One command was doing that. /gather referred to your networking events database by a name the setup reference never declared, so on some instances it could stop rather than log your event. That name is now declared and /gather resolves it.

The more useful half is the check behind it: a new build check refuses to ship any command that names something your workspace has no way to provide. It was written after a change prepared earlier today carried exactly that kind of dead reference into every command. That change never reached anyone — it was caught and withdrawn first — but it was caught by someone looking, not by any check. Now a check catches it.

Nothing you do changes and there is nothing to do on your side. No XP value, level threshold, badge criterion or unlock rule changed.

patches.title: v2.0.2 — One command opens web pages now, instead of four pretending to
patches.player_facing_summary:
Four commands could tell you about a web page they never actually opened.

/scout, /quest, /recruit and /gather all need to read a live page sometimes. Each carried its own idea of how to do it, and none of them checked first whether a browser was even available in your session — so on a session without one they could describe research that never happened. /quest was the worst of it: it carried its own three-step fallback ladder, so it could succeed or fail by a route nothing had tested.

/browse was already the command that checks properly and tells you plainly when it cannot reach a page. Those four now hand it the page instead of guessing, and their own competing instructions are deleted rather than left sitting underneath. One command opens pages; the rest ask it to. /browse also now distinguishes 'no browser here' from 'browser fine, page unreachable' — a login wall, a dead link, a bot check — because the two need different things from you.

The rule underneath it applies everywhere: probe before claiming a capability, in either direction. Your agent should not tell you something is unavailable because of where it appears to be running, and should not tell you it worked because it usually does. It attempts the thing, reads the result, and reports what came back. That is written once into the shared boot card every command loads, rather than repeated in each one.

A build check now refuses to ship any command other than /browse that drives the browser itself, so this cannot quietly grow back.

Nothing you do changes and there is nothing to do on your side. No XP value, level threshold, badge criterion or unlock rule changed.

patches.title: v2.0.3 — Your setup notes now work in whichever agent you open next
patches.player_facing_summary: At the end of setup, /awaken writes a small file into your folder so your next session picks The System back up without you explaining it again. It used to write one file, named for whichever agent you installed from. Open that same folder in a different agent and it started cold, because the agents do not agree on the filename. It now writes both: AGENTS.md holds the content, CLAUDE.md is a one-line import of it. Nothing to do on your side — run /awaken again if you want the second file now, or it arrives on your next repair or migration run.

patches.title: v2.0.4 — Housekeeping: the package's own documentation now matches its tests
patches.player_facing_summary: Nothing changes in play. The System's package ships a README describing the automated checks that run before any release, and that description had fallen behind the checks themselves — it listed six when ten were running. It is now accurate, and a new check holds it there: if a future release adds a check without updating the list, the build fails rather than shipping a stale description. No XP, level, badge or unlock rule is affected, and nothing you have installed behaves differently.

patches.title: v2.0.5 — /armor tells you when it can't build a .docx, instead of handing you a broken one
patches.player_facing_summary: Reported by a player. /armor's final step told the agent to build your .docx "via the docx skill" — a skill The System does not ship, and which is simply absent in many sessions. With nothing there, agents reached for whatever document library was handy, and at least one player received a .docx that Microsoft Word refused to open at all. /armor now checks first: if a .docx builder is available it uses it, and if not it says so plainly and gives you the HTML, which opens in Word and can be saved as .docx from there. It will not substitute an untested library to fill the gap. Your CV master in Notion and the HTML export were never affected.
